To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclei from the brain tissue of neonatal and adult mice were isolated and incubated under conditions that were optimal for the synthesis of RNA.

the RNA synthesized by isolated brain nuclei was similar to RNA-poly(A)-associated products synthesized by intact cells and that the proportion of poly(A) associated with nuclear RNA was higher in neonatal than in mature brain tissue.

(i) RNA-polyadenylic acid was synthesized by nuclei isolated from mouse brain; (ii) the RNA synthesized by the nuclei was similar to that described for intact eucaryotic cells; and (iii) the RNA from neonatal nuclei had a higher proportion of polyadenylic-containing RNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of RNA synthesis in isolated brain nuclei from mice.
the synthesis of polyadenylic (poly(A)) acid associated with the RNA of brain nuclei.
the development of a cell-free system to study the synthesis of RNA-polyadenylic acid by isolated brain nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the poly(A) content of brain RNA is developmentally regulated and that this may be a reflection of the maturation of neuronal function.
the poly(A) content of the RNA synthesized by isolated brain nuclei is similar to that of RNA synthesized in the intact brain cell.

the brain nuclei, isolated from mouse tissue at various stages, synthesized RNA molecules associated with poly(A) under cell-free conditions and that this RNA-poly(A)-containing material was synthesized by a mechanism similar to that described for intact cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RNA synthesized by isolated brain nuclei is similar to that synthesized by intact eukaryotes and that the poly(A)-containg RNA is similar in amount and in properties to poly(A)-contaiing RNA described for other eukaryotes.
the RNA-poly(A)-associated products of isolated brain nuclei appear to be similar in many respects to the poly(A) associated products of intact brain cells.
poly(A) is synthesized in brain cell nuclei at all stages of postnatal maturation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
brain nuclei are capable of synthesizing RNA-poly(A).
RNA-poly(A), a molecule that has been associated with the control of protein synthesis in eukaryotic systems, is also synthesized under cell-free conditions by isolated neural tissue.
the RNA synthesized in the brain is similar to that found in other tissues.
